=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh: The new `git check-ignore -q --no-index -- "${MANIFEST_UNION_PATH}"` arm in the `' 1 2 '|' 1 3 ')` case (around line ~285-290 of the LAST RUN DIFF) | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The implementation uses `git check-ignore --no-index` against the working tree's `.gitignore`. During a merge, the working tree contains the unmerged state — when `.gitignore` is also conflicted (one side adds the manifest path, the other side removes it or adds different rules), the check passes if either side's rule matches the manifest, even though the resolved `.gitignore` after the conflict resolves may not contain that rule.
  WHY: Two conflict shapes are now common per PR — modify/delete on the manifest plus a parallel `.gitignore` edit that re-tracks it — and the fix's contract ("honoured deletion only when merged `.gitignore` ignores the manifest") overstates what the working-tree probe actually proves. The changelog fragment (`changelog.d/6608-manifest-modify-delete-conflict.md`) says "merged `.gitignore` ignores the manifest" but the code checks the working-tree `.gitignore` pre-resolution. The script then runs `git rm --cached` on the manifest while the `.gitignore` is still unmerged, so the eventual merge commit can end up with an untracked manifest alongside a resolved `.gitignore` that says it should be tracked — an inconsistent tree the resolver cannot fix, since it has no view of the manifest anymore.
- scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh: The `::error::Manifest union-merge: unhandled reason=…` line emitted by the new `elif [ -n "${_mu_unhandled_reason}" ]` branch (around line ~341 of the LAST RUN DIFF) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The diagnostic carries the kill-switch value (`CONFLICT_MANIFEST_UNION_ENABLED=…`) but not the actual `.gitignore` probe result.
  WHY: Operators triaging an `ai:resolver-escalated` or `identical_failure_cap` re-occurrence on a different manifest path have no signal beyond "not_gitignored" to know whether the merged tree simply doesn't ignore the manifest, the working tree is mid-conflict (see the CORRECTNESS finding above), or the path spelling differs (e.g. trailing whitespace, CRLF).
- Requirement: "Record in the PR that you ran it both ways." (heal issue #6608, "Fix constraints" section)
  Expected change site: PR description body and/or commit message accompanying the new regression tests in `tests/test_conflict_manifest_union_contract.py` and the fix in `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh`.
  Evidence of absence: The PR description in `PR INTENT CONTEXT` is the one-line "Automated implementation. Closes https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/6608". No commit message in the LAST COMMIT CHANGE SUMMARY records the pre-fix repro. The autofix comment in `pr_all_comments_context.txt` (`entry[1]`) does explicitly acknowledge the deferral: "TASK_GAP_DEFERRED: The requested PR-body record … cannot be completed here. This sandbox exposes only a synthetic single-commit history, so `HEAD^` was unavailable for the pre-fix run. The fixed-state suite passed 18/18." That deferral belongs on the PR record, not only on a bot comment, so reviewers and the next heal cycle see it. The regression tests themselves are valid — `test_manifest_modify_delete_conflict_is_resolved_deterministically` would fail on the pre-fix code (stages 1+2 fall through the `*' 2 '*' 3 '*` arm and leave the manifest in the resolver allowlist, so `result.returncode == 0` never holds and `CONFLICT_RESOLVED=true` is never written), and the two fail-closed tests fail because the pre-fix code never emitted the `::error::` line nor called `exit 1`.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  PROBLEM: The delete/modify path checks the working-tree `.gitignore` with `git check-ignore -q --no-index`, not the resolved merge result. If `.gitignore` is also conflicted, the working tree has one side's version, but the resolver will resolve it later. The manifest deletion decision is made before `.gitignore` is resolved.
  WHY: When both the manifest and `.gitignore` are conflicted, the script might honor a manifest deletion based on a `.gitignore` rule that the resolver later removes. The manifest stays deleted even though the resolved `.gitignore` does not ignore it. The resolver handles the `.gitignore` conflict but cannot reconsider the manifest decision already made.
